title: Infrared View of NGC 346 (Hubble)
caption: Star-forming region NGC 346, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 346 · constellation Tucana · about 210,000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: Image: NASA, ESA, Antonella Nota (STScI, ESA)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A cloudy blue region stretches roughly from the upper right to the lower left corner, filled with bright white newborn stars. This is NGC 346, a giant stellar nursery about 210,000 light-years away in the Small Magellanic Cloud, a neighboring dwarf galaxy. Its infant stars are still wrapped in gas and dust.

NGC 346 stands in for the many star-forming regions that existed a few billion years after the big bang, when the universe was making stars at a furious pace. Like those early regions, it is poor in elements heavier than hydrogen and helium and holds many young, massive stars. Their ultraviolet radiation and stellar winds can tear apart star-forming clouds and disrupt the disks where planets may form.

Hubble imaged the region to identify its optically bright stars. To see stars still hidden in dust, astronomers planned at the time to use the infrared cameras on the James Webb Space Telescope, expecting a census that might reveal as many as 10,000 young stars, many under a million years old.

understand.summary: Hubble's ACS took this image in visible and near-infrared light. NASA shows F555W in blue, a combination of F555W and F814W in green, and F814W in red.
understand.eye: Hubble recorded the optically bright stars here, while young stars still buried in dust need longer infrared wavelengths, invisible to the eye, to be found.

explore: Compared with the Small Magellanic Cloud, our galaxy holds about 25 percent more of the heavier elements. Earlier work with Spitzer and Herschel counted the massive young stars in NGC 346, those of eight solar masses or more. Webb was expected to reach stars below a solar mass, giving the full range of stellar masses in the region.
sources: NASA release: NASA’s Webb Telescope Will Provide Census of Fledgling Stars in Stellar Nursery
